From 659a37844abc00c3dc676bb1faed29c1dacbf59f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Date: Sat, 31 Jul 2021 09:40:27 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] scsi: bsg-lib: Fix commands without data transfer in
 bsg_transport_sg_io_fn()

Set ret to 0 after the initial permission checks to avoid leaking -EPERM
for commands without data transfer.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20210731074027.1185545-3-hch@lst.de
Fixes: 75ca56409e5b ("scsi: bsg: Move the whole request execution into the SCSI/transport handlers")
Signed-off-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Signed-off-by: Martin K. Petersen <martin.petersen@oracle.com>

diff --git a/block/bsg-lib.c b/block/bsg-lib.c
index 239ebf747141..ccb98276c964 100644
--- a/block/bsg-lib.c
+++ b/block/bsg-lib.c
@@ -72,6 +72,7 @@ static int bsg_transport_sg_io_fn(struct request_queue *q, struct sg_io_v4 *hdr,
 		job->bidi_bio = NULL;
 	}
 
+	ret = 0;
 	if (hdr->dout_xfer_len) {
 		ret = blk_rq_map_user(rq->q, rq, NULL, uptr64(hdr->dout_xferp),
 				hdr->dout_xfer_len, GFP_KERNEL);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `block/bsg-lib.c`**
- A new line `ret = 0;` was added after the initial permission checks in the function `bsg_transport_sg_io_fn`. This change ensures that the return value `ret` is set to 0 for commands that do not involve data transfer, preventing the function from leaking the error code `-EPERM`.

### Relationships
The modification in `bsg-lib.c` addresses a specific issue related to command handling in the SCSI block layer. By setting `ret` to 0, the patch fixes a bug where commands without data transfer incorrectly returned a permission error. This change is linked to a previous commit (identified by the hash `75ca56409e5b`), which moved the request execution into the SCSI/transport handlers, indicating that the current fix is a refinement of that earlier implementation.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (!capable(CAP_SYS_RAWIO))
    return -EPERM;
```
```c
ret = blk_rq_map_user(rq->q, rq, NULL, uptr64(hdr->dout_xferp),
    hdr->dout_xfer_len, GFP_KERNEL);
```
```c
if (ret)
    goto out_unmap_bidi_rq;
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because if the command does not involve data transfer, the return value `ret` is not reset to 0 after the permission checks. As a result, if the command is valid but has no data transfer, the function may inadvertently return the error code `-EPERM`, which indicates a permission error, instead of a successful execution.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
ret = 0;
```
Reason:
This line resets the return value `ret` to 0 after the initial permission checks. By doing this, it ensures that commands without data transfer do not leak the `-EPERM` error code, allowing the function to correctly indicate success for valid commands that do not require data transfer.
